# Matrix multiplication {#sec-matrixMultiplicationMath}


::: {style="margin-top: 1em; font-size: 125%; font-weight: 1000; text-align: center;"}
Asio facture azafady!
:::

Wasn't matrix multiplication defined in the previous chapter(@sec-matrixOperationCoding)? Yes, but they are called Hadamard product and element-wise multiplication. But also as it might happen throughout this book, the same terms and symbols could be used where the meaning depends on the context. Here, another multiplication, but this is **the most used and useful matrix multiplication**.

Matrix multiplication is something that we encounter all the time. Consider again the purchase matrix earlier (@sec-matrixMath). Rabe bought 6 bananas, 3 toko strawberries, and 0.5 kapoaka of voatsinefy. Rakoto bought 3 bananas, 1 toko of strawberries, no voatsinefy. Sanda bought  10 toko of strawberries. Finally, Dora bought 1 banana and 2 kapoaka of vaotsinefy. The data could be represented as a matrix $A$.

$$
A = \begin{pmatrix}
    6 & 3 & 0.5 \\
    3 & 1 & 0 \\
    0 & 10 & 0 \\
    1 & 0 & 2 \\
\end{pmatrix}
$$

Now assume one banana is 500 Ar, a toko of strawberries is 1000 Ar, and a kapoaka of voatsinefy is 2000 Ar.

- Rabe paid: $500 \times 6 + 1000 \times 3 + 2000 \times 0.5 = 7000$
- Rakoto paid: $500 \times 3 + 1000 \times 1 + 2000 \times 0 = 2500$  etc.

This formula above, called dot product, is what is done in a receipt. As usual, mathematicians, will note that $\cdot$ and call it a matrix multiplication. That is: if
$$
P =
\begin{pmatrix}
    500 \\
    1000 \\
    2000
\end{pmatrix}
$$
then
$$
A \cdot P
$$
will give a vector of three rows and one column. Each row represents how much each person paid.

The multiplication makes sense only if the number of columns in the first matrix is the same as the number of rows in the second matrix--otherwise there is no pairs to multiply.

## Formal {.unnumbered}

Matrix multiplication is an operation that takes two matrices and produces a single new matrix by taking the dot product of rows from the first matrix and columns from the second.

For matrix multiplication to be possible, the number of columns in the first matrix must equal the number of rows in the second matrix.

If Matrix $A$ has dimensions $m \times n$ and Matrix $B$ has dimensions $n \times p$:

Their product $C = A \cdot B$ is a matrix of dimension $m \times p$.
Each entry  $c_{i,j}$ in the product matrix $C$ represents the dot product of the $i^{th}$ row of $A$ and the $j^{th}$ column of $B$:

$$
    c_{i,j} = \sum_{k=1}^{n} a_{i,k} \cdot b_{k,j} = a_{i,1}b_{1,j} + a_{i,2}b_{2,j} + \dots + a_{i,n}b_{n,j}
$${#eq-dotProduct}^[A good example to practice summation notation (@sec-sum)].

## Examples {.unnumbered}
- The price of fruit differ among markets, in another market, the price of the fruits were and we combine both price in matrix with two columns
$$
Q =
\begin{pmatrix}
    500 & 600 \\
    1000  & 800 \\
    2000 & 2500
\end{pmatrix}
$$

The product $ A \cdot Q$ will give the total for each market
$$ A \cdot Q
\begin{pmatrix}
    6 & 3 & 0.5 \\
    3 & 1 & 0 \\
    0 & 10 & 0 \\
    1 & 0 & 2 \\
\end{pmatrix}
\cdot
\begin{pmatrix}
    500 & 600 \\
    1000  & 800 \\
    2000 & 2500
\end{pmatrix} =
\begin{pmatrix}
  7000 & 7250 \\
  2500 & 2600 \\
  10000 & 8000 \\
  4500 & 5600
\end{pmatrix}
$$


- Multiplication with identity matrix $I$^[also noted as $I_n$ to be explicit with the dimensions]
  $$ A \cdot I
\begin{pmatrix}
    6 & 3 & 0.5 \\
    3 & 1 & 0 \\
    0 & 10 & 0 \\
    1 & 0 & 2
\end{pmatrix}
\cdot
\begin{pmatrix}
    1 & 0 & 0 \\
    0 & 1 & 0 \\
    0 & 0 & 1
\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
    6 & 3 & 0.5 \\
    3 & 1 & 0 \\
    0 & 10 & 0 \\
    1 & 0 & 2
\end{pmatrix}
$$
This is like multiplying by one in the arithmetic operation.

## Tips and warning {.unnumbered}

- There is no equivalent for matrix division. Instead, a division is defined as a multiplication with the inverse^[the inverse of a matrix does not necessarily exist].
- The inverse of a matrix $A$ is denoted as $A^{-1}$ such that $A \cdot A^{-1} = I$. This
- A linear model is essentially a A x + b = y is a matrix multiplication A times
- It is essential to understand that multiplication, and one can do it by hand, however, R programming can do that with almost not cost (@sec-matrixOperationCoding).
